chapter: Fats Waller, marriage and Indian school tours
title: The Indian school tour, ending in Sitka, Alaska
summary: Moore describes organizing a tour of Indian schools with his group, including the Sitka band greeting and salmon dinner.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: So she went back to school, she went back to teaching and I had the opportunity to at one time, I was going to Washington, we go to Washington together, and I played at Blues Alley and then knowing we belong to the National Conference of Indians in Washington, we knew Helen Peterson who was the publicity director, and so they got together a tour between Helen Peterson and Will Rogers, Jr., and Bob Bennett who was the Commissioner of Indian Affairs. They cooked up a tour where I could get a group from New York, fly them to their jobs all over the country for the Indian high schools. My first stop was in Haskell from there we went to --

No, Kansas. And from there we went to Sheloko, that's in Arkansas, on the border of Arkansas and Oklahoma; went to Riverside, California; went to Phoenix Indian School; went to Salem, Oregon to the Chimauwen Indian School and I rigged up sort of a speech to psyche up the kids about staying in school.

And the group that I had, on bass I had Truck Parham and I had Red Richards on piano and Freddie Moore on drums and Joe Barofaldi on clarinet and myself. That was the group I took over and we had a lot of fun. Ida went with me all through the tour.
How long did the tour last?
Oh, about two weeks, about two weeks.
Oh, so you went to all these places in a two week span.
Yes, in -- oh, wait a minute, I'm mixing this with something else. No, I didn't even go on my tour that time, the Indian school tour.
Yeah, yeah, no, Ida wasn't there.

I'm thinking about another tour I took with the colleges that's the time in South Dakota--/ Ida went with me. But during the Indian school tour, we were going so fast, we went as far as Sitka, Alaska, up to the edge of the mountain. We flew from Seattle to Sitka and at Sitka when we were coming down to land at the airport, there was a band waiting and I had no idea where the band was from and the guys in the band said, 'I bet that's for you.' it's inconceivable to think that No, /there must be some other people on the

plane. So when the plane landed everybody was gone except us because I was sitting in the back, to get myself right and step down -- as soon as I stepped out, the band struck, that was music, and it was beautiful. And I went down the ramp and I stood in front of the band and asked them what they were playing, and they all had beautiful red uniforms, but the cutest thing I had seen in quite a long time was that I noticed they all looked alike in their red uniforms but their shoes; some would be wearing tennis shoes and some would be wearing boots and some would be wearing some other shoes, that was a funny thing. Of course, I laughed but I didn't let them know what I was laughing at and I thanked them and each one of them, I shook their hands, and they had a band of about 40 pieces and that was one of my memorable occasions in the tour and we were invited to all kinds of parties there. After the concert the chef invited us over to the school dining hall. He gave us a salmon dinner, it was beautiful -- great big pieces of two-inch/thick salmon. There was so much.
